text:
maya: heads-up — starting ~08:15 UTC we're seeing a big tail-latency regression from eu-central-1 for the text-gen endpoints. p99s jumped from ~40ms to ~350-450ms. No obvious customer deploys. anyone seen this?

liam: seeing it too. traces point to increased time between request accept and first token write. network timings look noisy for a subset of hosts in eu-pop-1.

jessica: quick metrics dump from prod-prometheus:```
redwood_inference_latency_p50{region="eu-central-1"} 0.032
redwood_inference_latency_p95{region="eu-central-1"} 0.118
redwood_inference_latency_p99{region="eu-central-1"} 0.412
kv_cache_hit_rate{region="eu-central-1"} 0.28 # down from 0.92 at 08:10
request_batch_size_avg{route="/v1/generate"} 4.1 -> 2.7
```

maya: interesting — KV cache hit rate collapsing at the same time as tail spike. could be cache eviction or a change in kernel selection that invalidated cache layout?

ankur: we rolled kernel-selector v2.3 to dedicated/eu nodes at 07:50 UTC (canary -> 50%). v2.3 changed LRU bucket sizing and added a different alignment for KV pages to improve GPU kernel throughput.

liam: if kernel-selector changed alignment, it could change KV key layout leading to more cache misses and smaller batches (seen in metrics). smaller batch sizes + cache misses = more per-request setup and higher latency.

felix: I ran mtr from an affected host to the provider edge earlier:```
Start: 2024-06-10T08:22:00Z
 1. host.local  0.3ms
 2. edge1.provider  1.2ms
 3. provider-pop  55.6ms  packet loss 20%
 4. backbone  60-130ms jitter
```
looks like provider POP issues too — packet loss and jitter correlate with the time window.

jessica: also noticed dns latency spikes for model-manifest endpoints around same time (avg lookup 5ms -> 120ms). could be provider DNS resolver issues causing model manifest fetch delays and forcing runtime fallback to cold path (rebuild KV).

maya: summary hypothesis: kernel-selector v2.3 rollout changed KV alignment -> increased cache misses; simultaneously eu provider POP had packet loss/jitter causing manifest/durable store fetch delays; combined effect reduced batching and increased per-request setup -> tail spike.

ankur: agreed. immediate mitigation options: roll back kernel-selector v2.3 in eu, increase KV cache capacity on eu nodes, apply aggressive local manifest caching TTL, and open ticket with network provider for POP packet loss.

liam: starting rollback to v2.2 on the 50% of eu dedicated hosts now. will also flip KV cache autosize to +30% for eu-pop-1.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback job queued (job 8273). expected completion ~08:35 UTC. :arrows_counterclockwise:

felix: opened ticket with provider (TICKET-9987) and attached mtr/traceroute and loss graphs.

jessica: after rollback p99 dropped to ~55ms and kv_cache_hit_rate recovered to ~89% within 8m. batching avg went back to 4.0. monitoring for recurrence.

maya: great triage. follow-ups: (1) add a perf test in canary that validates KV alignment invariants when kernel-selector changes, (2) add synthetic manifest fetch metrics to catch provider DNS/POP issues earlier, (3) document noisy-neighbor checks for provider POPs. I'll create tickets. :white_check_mark:

liam: also recommend running a short bleed test with v2.3 on a small subset of non-prod eu hosts with synthetic KV-heavy traffic to exercise alignment change.

maya: noted. thanks everyone — keeping this thread open until provider confirms fix and rollback is fully validated.
